title: Elementary length and time are tiny and their ratio is light speed

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Elementary length and time are tiny and their ratio is light speed

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Each connection in the causal network of the universe corresponds to an identical elementary distance (perhaps about 10^-35 meters) and elementary time (perhaps about 10^-43 seconds), whose ratio is a fixed speed identified with the speed of light.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: One may guess that this elementary distance is around 10^(-35) meters, and that the elementary time interval is around 10^(-43) seconds. But whatever these values are, a crucial point is that their ratio must be a fixed speed, and we can identify this with the speed of light.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Space, Time and Relativity” (from p. 516), p. 520. Scope: discrete structure of spacetime

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-20: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical scales and light-speed relation can generate empirical predictions in concrete models. Present data provide indirect bounds but cannot measure the elementary intervals or establish that all causal links have identical lengths.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Derive dispersion, Lorentz-symmetry, or propagation signatures of fixed elementary length and time intervals and fit them to high-energy and gravitational observations. A common discreteness scale whose ratio gives c would support the claim; incompatible scales or anisotropic propagation would refute the stated form.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Current null tests only constrain model-dependent effects.

Fixed lattice intervals need not produce a unique observable signature.

Planck-scale intervals are far below direct resolution.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical guesses are the Planck scales, which follow at once from public constants, and the ratio of those defined scales is c. That checks the arithmetic and the identification Wolfram states. It does not test whether causal-network edges have those lengths, because no dataset contains a discreteness scale.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compute the Planck length and Planck time from measured c, G, and hbar and compare them with the stated 10^-35 m and 10^-43 s, and check that their ratio equals c. Agreement of the ratio and of the order of magnitude is required by the definitions; a measured elementary length far from the Planck length would refute the numerical guess.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Once every causal edge is assigned one elementary length and one elementary time, their ratio is a fixed speed by definition and is identified with c rather than measured.

No experiment measures an elementary length near 10^-35 m; current data only leave that scale allowed.
